content.text:
My first fix only covered half the problem. This time I traced the whole flow: the AI prompt, saving, the database and the screen that shows the recap. The other cause was in the prompt.

**What was wrong:** the app creates a default "General" mode and turns it on, so recaps nearly always use the mode prompt, not the default one I fixed last time. That mode prompt said nothing about tasks without dates. Its "Action items" section only says "Tasks and follow-ups identified." So the model treated "Priya will send the contract" as too vague and left it out. Saving, the database and the recap screen don't drop anything.

**What I changed:**
- **Mode prompt** (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`): any section about tasks, follow-ups or next steps now has to include every task someone took on, even with no date. Items are written as "Priya: send the contract", and a date is added only if someone said one. I put the rule in the code that builds the prompt, not in the section text, because section text is saved in each user's database and editing it wouldn't change existing installs.
- **Groq prompt** (`electron/llm/prompts.ts`): this one is used on the default path when Groq is the model. Its only example had a deadline ("by Wednesday"), so I added the same rule.
- The deadline filter I removed last time stays removed.

**One thing still drops other people's tasks:** in the Sales and Team Meeting modes, the action items section says "All action items that were said **I** would do after the meeting", and Recruiting's says "that I have to do". In those modes the model is told to list only your own tasks, so Priya's would still be skipped, by design. If you use one of those, I can change the wording to cover everyone's tasks. That means a database migration so existing modes get the new text too.

I haven't type-checked or run this because `node_modules` isn't installed here. To test, rebuild, end a short meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract", and look for "Priya: send the contract" in the recap. The log line `[MeetingPersistence] Active mode: ...` shows which mode and prompt were used.
